messages.subject: nested render* calls
parts:
I've recently been building Shiny apps that alter their UI based on the user's input.
An example of how to do this was posted by W. Chang here: https://gist.github.com/wch/5436415/.
In that example, explicit outputs are created and named dynamically, via a call like `output[[plotname]] <- renderPlot(...)`.
Lazy evaluation then prevents any plots from being drawn than don't have the corresponding dynamic `plotOutput(plotname)` in the UI (populated via `renderUI`).

Below is an alternative that seems to be working for me and is much simpler in code, but perhaps more complicated when modeling out the reactive dependency chains:

##------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(shiny); library(DT)

buildTabPanel <- function(title) {
    tabPanel(title = title, DT::renderDataTable(iris))
}

ui <- fluidPage(sliderInput("n_tabs", label = "# Tabs", min = 1, max = 5, value = 2),
                uiOutput("outer"))

server <- function(input,output) {
    output$outer <- renderUI({
        tab_panels <- lapply(seq_len(input$n_tabs), function(i) buildTabPanel(i))
        do.call(tabsetPanel, tab_panels)
    })
}
##------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The `ui` holds the "outer" placeholder.
Then, the server's `renderUI` function dynamically builds each `tabPanel` (based on `input$n_tabs`) and populates it with a `renderDataTable`.
I was surprised this worked at all during my experimentation, but happily delighted that it did.
My only concern is that perhaps I've stumbled upon a design pattern that can cause problems with the reactive evaluation chain (since I'm not well-versed in the exact implementation details of the render* and other reactive functions).
Does anyone see any alarming flaws with this pattern?

Cheers,

-murat

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: nested render* calls
parts: That's mostly fine. If you put a DT::renderDataTable() call (or most any other render call) directly in a server-generated UI, Shiny will implicitly insert a corresponding dataTableOutput() call for you in that location (with a randomly generated ID). This functionality was introduced to support Shiny R Markdown documents. It does mean creating many outputs; while any outputs that aren't showing will be suspended (which you referred to as lazy evaluation), they can't be garbage collected because Shiny doesn't know for a fact that they're not coming back later. So you do have to watch out for memory leaks with this pattern.

messages.author: f45657ea067c43ec
messages.subject: Re: nested render* calls
parts:
Ah, I see your point, thanks much for the insight. I now see why in the original Gist example uses the 'maximum number of outputs' design pattern.

Now purely wondering/conjecture for sake of discussion: would it conceptually be possible (i.e. easily within the existing Shiny code) to 'link' those auto-generated output IDs with a 'parent' output ID (or a random state-identifying token associated with the parent)?
Then, when the parent output is recomputed (and the token changes), all token-associated children are destroyed, gc()-ed, and then re-built dynamically (and linked to the new stateful token) as needed.
It'd be _almost_ as if the auto-generated output objects take a reactive dependency to the parent output object, with a special reactive destroying/gc()-ing behavior.

-m
